name: Meta
summary: A 45-minute technical screen, then a full loop of several conversations covering coding, design and how you work.

sources.title: Preparing for your full loop interview

process.note: Meta's prep pages confirm the 45-minute screen and a multi-conversation full loop. The round mix inside the loop is what candidates commonly report and depends on level.

stages.name: Recruiter call
stages.detail: Candidates typically report a short call about background, level and timeline.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.detail: A 45-minute conversation with an engineer, designed to assess technical skills.

stages.name: Full loop
stages.detail: Several conversations that assess technical skills and help hiring managers get to know you. Candidates often report two coding rounds at a brisk pace.
rounds: System or product design, senior roles (reported)

stages.name: Decision
stages.detail: Feedback is typically gathered and reviewed before an offer decision and team matching.

design.note: Design rounds are commonly reported for experienced roles, often about large social products and their data flow.

values.title: Meta core values
values.summary: Meta publishes a short list of core values that it says guide daily decisions. The names below are Meta's; the explanations are ours.

items.name: Move fast
items.gist: Act with urgency and clear blockers so the most important work ships sooner.

items.name: Build awesome things
items.gist: Aim past good enough towards work that genuinely impresses people.

items.name: Be direct and respect your colleagues
items.gist: Have the hard conversation honestly while assuming others are experts too.

items.name: Focus on long-term impact
items.gist: Pick the problems that matter most even when the payoff is years away.

items.name: Live in the future
items.gist: Use and shape the tools you are building before everyone else does.

items.name: Meta, Metamates, me
items.gist: Put the company and your team ahead of personal credit.

prompts.text: Tell a story where you cut scope or removed a blocker to ship something important quickly.
Describe a time you gave or received blunt feedback. How did you keep it respectful?
Talk about a choice where you traded a quick win for a better long-term result.
Share a moment when helping your team mattered more than your own project.
